tldr: Extreme heat forced organisers to cut the stage from 189.7km to 110.2km; Wout van Aert won a five-up sprint in Córdoba from the day's decisive breakaway, while the GC group came home 2:44 back together with every top-ten position unchanged from stage 14.

narrative.headline: Van Aert outsprints Romele and Nys as a shortened Córdoba stage goes to the break
narrative.body:
With Andalusian temperatures forecast to soar, organisers shortened the stage from 189.7km to 110.2km overnight, cutting the early rolling terrain but leaving the closing Puerto Artafi climb and Córdoba's finishing circuit intact. An early move of roughly a dozen riders formed inside the first 10km and was allowed only a minute or so by the Visma-led bunch; on the Puerto Artafi, with around 33km to go, Andreas Leknessund attacked clear of that group, was joined first by Ramses Debruyne and then, moments later, by Wout van Aert, Thibau Nys and Alessandro Romele, instantly turning the gap to the peloton decisive.

The five worked cleanly to the finish and reached Córdoba's closing circuit together, with Van Aert shutting down every late dig through the streets to set up a straight sprint. Nys opened it first, using Van Aert as an unwitting lead-out before the Belgian came around him in the final metres to beat Romele and Nys, taking his third stage win of this Vuelta and further points towards the green jersey. Behind, the GC contenders were content to sit up and conserve energy a day after Pandera's fireworks, rolling home together 2:44 down with no changes among the overall favourites.

gcImpact.headline: GC frozen: Mas's lead over Gall and Roglič holds unchanged
gcImpact.body: With the breakaway taking the stage and the GC group finishing together, every position in the top ten carried over unchanged from stage 14. Enric Mas leads Felix Gall by 2:06 and Primož Roglič by 2:10, with Richard Carapaz fourth at 4:24 and Oscar Onley fifth at 5:44 as the race heads into its final week.

riderPerformances.name: Wout van Aert
riderPerformances.narrative: Van Aert made the day's decisive move on the Puerto Artafi with roughly 33km to go, jumping across to Leknessund and Debruyne alongside Nys and Romele, and never had to work especially hard to stay away once the quintet formed, with the peloton behind giving the move its blessing the day after the Sierra de la Pandera summit finish. In Córdoba's finishing circuit he shut down every late attack, then used Nys's early sprint as an inadvertent lead-out to come around him in the final metres for his third stage win of this Vuelta and more points towards a green jersey he already holds comfortably.
